title: udlm_finding — a detected condition, as a sealed interpretation
description:
Drift, tamper, staleness, a missed cadence — represented as a SEALED LEDGER INTERPRETATION with a lifecycle, never as a field on the working record (ADR-060).

WHY NOT A FIELD ON THE RECORD. A finding is an INTERPRETATION: someone compared two things and concluded something. Storing `drift: true` on the record mixes a fact with a judgment about the fact, and then cannot answer who concluded it, when, or on what evidence. It would also be a stored derivable and a lineage claim in the state store — both of which the claims discipline forbids (ADR-059).

CURRENT STATUS IS DERIVED ON READ, ALWAYS. A finding says 'was detected'; it never says 'is drifted'. Asking a finding for current status is asking a historical record a present-tense question, and it will answer confidently and wrongly the moment the condition clears.

THE LEDGER HOLDS THE WHOLE STORY AS ONE CITATION WALK: divergence version -> finding -> disposition -> resolution version.

_schemaURL.description: OpenLineage: the schema defining this facet. Pinned to this file.

finding_class.description: What KIND of condition was detected. Distinct classes carry distinct response postures — tamper is not drift, and treating them alike would route a suspected compromise into a reconciliation queue. One mechanism, one routing home, one lifecycle; a profile MAY add a class, entering by the curation ladder like any other governed term.

finding_key.description: OPENED ONCE, keyed on resource plus the diverged field set. A second detection of the same divergence CONFIRMS the finding rather than opening another — without this, a condition that recurs every reconciliation cycle produces a finding per cycle, and the signal drowns in its own repetition. Flap debounce is policy; the key is what makes debounce possible at all.

subject.description: The record the finding is about, with the version and chain head at detection — so the evidence stays checkable after the record moves on.

diverged_fields.description: The dot-paths that differed. Part of the key, and the reason a finding is specific enough to close: 'this resource has drifted' cannot be resolved, 'these three fields differ' can.

state.description: A finding is opened by its detection seal and CLOSED BY A RESOLUTION SEAL THAT CITES IT — reconverged, accepted, or reviewed. Two states, because a finding is not a workflow: the disposition lives in the closing seal, so adding states here would duplicate what the citation walk already tells you.

closed_by.description: The resolution seal that closed this finding.

disposition.description: `reconverged` = the divergence was removed; `accepted` = it stands and is now intended; `reviewed` = looked at, no action. Three different facts about the same condition, and an operator needs to tell them apart later.
